newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KOHLER INSPIRES DORTMUND TO EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KOHLER INSPIRES DORTMUND TO EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund braved a Manchester United onslaught at the same time as riding their luck to deservedly clinch a place in the European Cup Final for the first time in their history on Wednesday.

Their 1-0 win over United at Old Trafford gave them the semifinal tie 2-0 on aggregate and also gives them the chance to become the first team from the Bundesliga to become European champions since Hamburg in 1983.

United, bidding to reach the final for the first time since 1968, did just about everything but score - and even when Ole Solskjaer had the ball in the net in the second minute and Andy Cole in the last, the two goals were disallowed.

Instead, the one that counted came from Lars Ricken after only eight minutes and from that time on the German champions, missing injured European Footballer of the Year Matthias Sammer as well as four other internationals, had the psychological advantage, if not the territorial.

Ricken collected a through ball from Dortmund's outstanding captain Andreas Moeller wide on the right, left defender Gary Pallister standing with a lightening turn and sprint, and buried his cross-shot deep in the far corner despite a despairing attempted save from goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel.
That left United needing three goals to win and they had three clear-cut chances to score before the break through Eric Cantona, Andy Cole and Pallister.

After 17 minutes Cantona took too long to control the ball two metres from goal after goalkeeper Stefan Klos spooned a Cole shot straight to him, and when he did finally shoot, the long leg of man-of-the-match Juergen Kohler, got in the way.
It was a poignant victory for Kohler, who was injured on this ground playing for Germany in the opening game of Euro'96 which forced him to miss the remainder of the tournament.
Pallister missed with a wide open goal at his mercy after 35 minutes when he headed the wrong side of the post, and Cole shot wide with only Klos to beat just before halftime.
United kept up the pressure in the second half and in all had 21 goal attempts.

Although United manager Alex Ferguson was unimpressed with Dortmund's organisation afterwards, only outstanding defending from Kohler and the rest of the defence and impressive covering by Austrian sweeper Wolfgang Feiersinger kept United at bay.
Dortmund often had eight or nine men behind the ball and only broke free of United's pressure occasionally during a frantic second half as the home team became ever more desperate to score.
A delighted Dortmund manager Ottmar Hitzfeld conceeded afterwards no team had ever subjected Dortmund to so much pressure.
"I expected a whirlwind to break over us and that is exactly what happened," he said.

"United played a fantastic game themselves -- only they did not score. We had a lot of luck on our side and you need that sometimes to win. The early goal allowed us to relax slightly and gave us the pyschological advantage and this was a huge victory for us as we were missing five internationals."

Ferguson said: "Sometimes you only improve after losing, but I cannot criticise my players. They have given their all, but I accept that from the number of chances we made tonight we should have scored.
"I think that like all German sides Dortmund never gave up, but I cannot say their organisation was great. Just look at the chances we created."

United are likely to be back in the Champions' League next season by winning the English title but the Germans will most likely have to beat Juventus in Munich on May 28 because they have dropped behind in the race for German crown.
